messages:
Mara: Heads up — saw a couple of requests routed to the wrong tenant in prod. Traced it to X-Run-Context being ignored and UA-based routing kicking in. Anyone seen this behavior recently?

Dennis: We added a UA inference fallback a while back for older SDKs that don't set X-Run-Context. It should only apply when the header is absent. Do you have an example request?

Mara: Yep, pasted the raw headers from the proxy logs:

```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-prod
X-Run-Context: tenant=acme;ts=1853054321
User-Agent: Redwood/cli-v0.8
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx
```

Mara: Proxy log shows we routed to default-pool (tenant: public) because the header was treated as untrusted. infra-bot shows: "edge-proxy: X-Run-Context missing-signature -> applying UA-route 'cli' -> default-pool"

infra-bot: edge-proxy[edge-237]: route decision: header(X-Run-Context)=present but unsigned -> fallback to UA heuristics.

Olga: Ah — this is the unsigned-header safety check we added to prevent header spoofing from the open edge. The rule currently is: Authorization context (bearer) wins, then signed X-Run-Context, then UA inference, then IP. Seems the incoming token was a serverless key with limited tenant mapping so it fell back.

Mara: But the request had a valid bearer for tenant acme. Why did auth not win? Token looks like a single-service token (no tenant claim) for our internal bridge. We rely on X-Run-Context in that flow. That token is expected for proxy-to-proxy calls where the header conveys downstream tenant.

Dennis: Right — we have two overlapping assumptions. For internal bridge flow we allow trusted headers, but only if they are signed to avoid spoofing when requests cross customer-facing edges.

Olga: Proposal: 1) formalize header precedence as: authorization claims -> signed X-Run-Context (HMAC + kid) -> unsigned X-Run-Context only from trusted source IP ranges -> UA inference -> other fallbacks. 2) add X-Run-Sig header format and timestamp tolerance.

Mara: Example spec for header signing I sketched:

```
X-Run-Context: tenant=acme;ts=1853054321;kid=v2
X-Run-Sig: hmac_sha256_base64(kid_secret, "tenant=acme;ts=1853054321")
```

Mara: Timestamp tolerance: 2 minutes by default. If signature missing or invalid, we should record a metric and continue falling back rather than hard-fail.

Dennis: Agreed on metrics. Add counters: route.header.signed.accept, route.header.signed.reject, route.header.unsigned.fallback. We'll surface them in Console as a per-route breakdown.

sre-jen: A few operational points: key rotation (kid) must be supported and cached in the edge with TTL. Rotations will be frequent for some customers — caching + versioned kid solves that. Also we need to ensure KMS access latency doesn't add to request tail latency; fetch async and fall back to short-cache misses with token-only routing.

Olga: For rollout: add a gateway feature flag gate: header-sig-verify. Default off. Rollout plan: enable for internal prod traffic only -> 10% customer traffic EU region -> increase to 50% with alerts -> full global roll. During each stage we track the metrics Dennis mentioned plus 'route.override.count' and 'route.sig.failure_rate'.

Mara: Sounds good. Can we also add a small safeguard: when X-Run-Context is unsigned but bearer token maps to a known bridge service, accept it? That allows internal infra to continue while we onboard customers to signed headers.

Olga: Yes, we can whitelist known service client IDs (short term). Long term we want signed headers + kid. Add header schema to docs and SDKs.

Dennis: I'll open a PR for the gateway changes and the metric exports. Planning to add config like: 

```
gateway:
  header_precedence:
    - auth
    - signed_xrun
    - trusted_ip_unsigned_xrun
    - user_agent
    - ip
  signature:
    tolerance_seconds: 120
    required_for_public: true
```

deploy-bot: Created PR #1234 for gateway: header-sig-verification + metrics export (link: https://git.internal/pr/1234) :white_check_mark:

Mara: Awesome. Can we also add a Console dashboard tile that shows per-route header-sig acceptance ratio and a small alert if sig_failure_rate > 0.5% over 5m?

Dennis: Yep, will add dashboard widget and alert playbook.

sre-jen: One more: CLI SDK owners — we should ensure the CLI adds the signed X-Run-Sig on next release and supports kid header. I'll ping the SDK channel.

Olga: Action items: Dennis -> PR + metrics; Mara -> doc sample + integration tests; Jen -> key rotation plan + cache TTL; Dennis/Olga -> rollout plan and feature flag schedule.

Mara: Thanks all :thumbsup:

Dennis: 👍

Olga: :rocket:
